title: Drug Discovery and Molecular Simulation
answer: Protein structure, new molecules, simulated trials, toxicity forecasting and repurposing.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Protein Structure Prediction
children.blurb: Protein structure prediction is the computational task of inferring a protein's three-dimensional folded shape from its amino acid sequence.

children.name: Designing New Molecules
children.blurb: Designing new molecules with AI means using machine learning to propose chemical structures that have a desired biological activity, such as binding to a target protein, while also being synthesizable and safe.

children.name: Simulated Clinical Trials
children.blurb: Simulated clinical trials use computational models of patients, diseases, and treatments to predict how a drug might perform before or instead of a traditional human trial.

children.name: Toxicity Forecasting
children.blurb: Toxicity forecasting uses machine learning to predict whether a candidate molecule will cause harm in a biological system before it enters costly laboratory or animal testing.

children.name: Drug Repurposing
children.blurb: Drug repurposing is the practice of finding new therapeutic uses for medicines that are already approved or have passed early safety testing.

sections.body: This field uses machine learning to find and improve drug candidates before they reach a person. AI now predicts how a chain of amino acids folds into a three-dimensional protein, which helps researchers see where a drug might bind. It also generates new molecular structures with desired properties, such as binding strength or solubility. Simulated trials use existing patient data to model how a drug might perform in a group, before any real human is enrolled. Toxicity forecasting flags molecules likely to harm the liver, heart, or other organs. Drug repurposing screens approved medicines against new disease targets to find existing drugs that might work for another condition.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are mature enough for routine use, while others remain experimental. Protein structure prediction has become reliable for many single proteins, but complexes and flexible regions still cause errors. Molecule generation can propose many candidates quickly, yet most fail later in lab tests because predicted binding does not guarantee real activity. Simulated clinical trials can reproduce some historical results, but they cannot replace human trials for safety or efficacy. Toxicity models catch common problems but miss rare or delayed effects. Drug repurposing has found a few successes, but the hit rate is low and most candidates do not advance.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to understand the starting point should begin with Protein Structure Prediction, because every later step depends on knowing the shape of the target. Designing New Molecules follows from that shape and shows how AI proposes compounds to fit it. Toxicity Forecasting sits beside molecule design, since a promising molecule is useless if it is unsafe. Simulated Clinical Trials moves the work from a computer model of a molecule to a computer model of a patient group, testing whether the candidate might work in a population. Drug Repurposing is a shortcut that skips new molecule design entirely and asks whether an existing approved drug can be redirected. Together these pages move from structure to design to safety to population testing to reuse.
